pages.text: The waves washed in and rolled back out. Riri and Lolo ran onto the sand.
They wanted to build a castle that would stay up when the waves came. "Today our castle will stand until evening!"
Riri poked the sand with a finger. Lolo scooped up dry sand with both hands. "We have to choose only wet sand." "Lots of sand will make it strong."
Riri picked out wet sand, one handful at a time. The castle wasn't even ankle-high yet.
The sun began to sink. In front of Riri was just a little pile of carefully chosen sand.
Lolo piled dry sand into a mountain. A gust of wind blew.
The mountain collapsed in a heap. Lolo's boots were buried deep in sand.
A wave washed in and rolled back out. The sand it left behind was smooth and shiny.
They pressed that sand firmly into place with their hands. Even when a wave reached their feet, the castle stayed up.
A crab came scuttling sideways. It slipped through the castle gate and sat down. Riri and Lolo looked at each other and burst out laughing.
